findings: Exceptional module library with 41 modules published in the Private Module Registry
Outstanding versioning practices: average 16.76 versions per module indicates active maintenance and maturity
Comprehensive provider coverage across HashiCorp ecosystem: vault (15), terraform (13), boundary (1), nomad (1), waypoint (2), consul (1), hvs (1), vaultradar (1), autobahn (1), util (3)
99.8% module health: 40 modules fully operational, only 2 modules with minor ingestion failures on specific versions
Demo platform context: This organization demonstrates best-in-class module development practices typical of HashiCorp internal demo/reference platforms
Module categories include: secrets management, encryption, PKI, dynamic credentials, policy automation, infrastructure provisioning, developer platforms, and integration patterns
Strong semantic versioning discipline: Most modules have reached 1.x.x stable releases, indicating production-ready quality
config-driven-import module shows extensive iteration with 68 versions (0.1.0 → 1.3.3), demonstrating continuous improvement
Cross-product integration modules present: vault-and-ansible, terraform-and-ansible, kubernetes-vso, demonstrating ecosystem integration maturity
recommendations: Document module usage patterns: Create internal documentation showing which demo scenarios use which modules to help other teams adopt similar patterns
Consider extracting reusable modules to HashiCorp public registry: Several modules (e.g., vcs-workflow, workspaces-projects-rbac, policy-as-code) could benefit the broader community
Implement module health monitoring: Set up alerts for registry ingestion failures (2 modules have failed versions: all-boundary-use-cases v0.1.1, invisimart-waypoint-template-nocode-ecs v1.0.1)
Add module adoption metrics: Track which modules are most commonly used across HashiCorp's demo ecosystem to identify high-value candidates for public release
Establish module lifecycle policy: Define deprecation and archival processes for modules that are no longer maintained (if any become obsolete)

scoring_breakdown.module_count_rationale: 41 modules far exceeds typical production org PMR (5-15 modules), demonstrating comprehensive standardization. Full 10/10 points.
scoring_breakdown.versioning_rationale: Average 16.76 versions per module indicates exceptional CI/CD integration and active maintenance. Most modules have 10+ versions showing iterative improvement. Full 10/10 points.
scoring_breakdown.provider_coverage_rationale: Strong coverage across HashiCorp products (vault, terraform, boundary, nomad, waypoint, consul) plus custom providers (autobahn, util). Deducted 2 points for limited coverage of public cloud providers (aws, azure, gcp) - though this is expected for a HashiCorp internal demo platform focused on product capabilities. 8/10 points.
scoring_breakdown.module_health_rationale: 99.8% of module versions are healthy (685/687 published versions). Only 2 version ingestion failures across 2 modules, both with workarounds in place. Near-perfect health. 9/10 points.
scoring_breakdown.total_rationale: 37/40 points = 92.5%. This organization demonstrates 'Standardized' PMR maturity typical of mature Platform Engineering teams. The high module count, exceptional versioning practices, and multi-product coverage indicate this is a best-practice reference implementation.

context.comparison_to_typical_org: This organization's PMR maturity (41 modules, 16.76 avg versions) is 3-5x higher than typical enterprise production organizations (8-15 modules, 3-5 avg versions). This is expected for a HashiCorp internal demo platform that showcases best practices across multiple products.
context.business_impact: Exceptional module library enables rapid demo environment provisioning, consistent customer-facing demonstrations, and serves as a reference architecture for customer implementations.
